moveEvidence.speaker: Richard Swinburne
moveEvidence.claim: God creates persons before he can ask their consent and supposes they would prefer a life benefiting others through suffering; more broadly, God permits rather than directly causes atrocity, and vulnerability makes historical choices significant.
moveEvidence.warrant: On the consent challenge, persons do not yet exist to be asked and Swinburne supposes they would choose useful suffering; across centuries, consequential antisemitic choices require possible harm, while removing that significance would preserve lives but remove serious responsibility.
moveEvidence.inference: Lack of prior consent does not defeat the account if the hypothesized preference and whole-world value of consequential responsibility are accepted.
